summary: Bulk files. The Files tree chooses many rows (a click, a range, add or take away one; a click that only adds does not move the board; the choice outlives the tree's readings). With two or more files of your home chosen, a band under the tab's header says how many and where, with Move to…, Copy to…, Delete and Choose none; the right-click on a chosen row offers the same for all of them plus "A utility on copies of these…"; dragging a chosen row onto a folder moves them all. One press runs one batch (new Kernel ops files.batch / files.batch_undo / files.batch_plan / files.batches in workbench/bulk_files.py) on the floor's worker, recorded as one change with every file's before and after; the line under the tab's header says it with ONE Undo for the batch, which puts back what can be and names what cannot (moved away since, old place taken, a copy changed, restored from DELETE before). DELETE (the room) lists what was deleted together with "put them back". A line can end in "move to FOLDER", "copy to FOLDER" or "delete": the line before it reads as every line reads (an @files:<folder> source reads that folder's entries), and the console shows a step that asks (count, folder, first five names, what is left out) with the press and "not now"; its answer carries "undo the batch". home_reach applies (nothing lands or is taken outside your home or Files; Delete is the system's bin). The K6 sandbox takes a folder's worth (64 inputs, it was 8, all together within 128 MB = what 8 of the largest made before; 64 outputs within its 32 MB), and its Apply offers "Undo the apply" (sandbox.undo, approve): files it made new into DELETE, revisions it replaced back from the kept versions, read back and recorded; anything changed since is left and named (state PUT BACK).

decisions: Interpretation of "one line": the one Undo line under the Files tab's header (L6b's Note) says the whole batch with one Undo; the Kernel journals one request per batch.

The language stays read-only: the act step is taken off the end of the line (bulk_files.split_act) before language.run's read; the change is files.batch on the owner's press, never a pipeline transform.

A line whose source is @files:<a folder> reads that folder's entries (files.list … | pick entries) only when it ends in move/copy/delete; the same line without the act still reads the folder's own row as before (no change to the @files address for other lines).
The plan reads up to 1000 rows (language.run caps at 200) so a folder's worth (205 in Downloads) can be acted on; a batch takes at most 1000 paths (the Kernel's array bound).

Undo of a batch never forces: a moved file is put back only if the same inode is still at its new place and its old place is free; a copy goes to DELETE only if unchanged (inode, size, time); a deletion restored from DELETE since counts as back already; a folder the batch made is removed again only when empty.
Move to a folder that is not there: a line's plan offers to make it first (one level, its parent must exist); the tree's Move to… picks an existing folder.

Undo of an Apply puts the files Apply made new into DELETE (restorable, L6b's convention for new folders and copies) rather than unlinking them; sandbox.undo is approve scope (your press), not in ALWAYS_ASKS (it only puts back).

The sandbox's total input size is kept at 8 x INPUT_BYTES (128 MB): "raised from 8 to 64 within its size limit". MOST_OUTPUTS raised 32 -> 64 so a folder's worth of renamed files can be offered (still within OUTPUT_BYTES).

Speed: a batch's checks read the system's places once (bulk_files.Reach) and the identity store is updated in one pass (carry_all); files_service.may_change is asked only for her work (for your press it never refuses, by its own rules). In the window the 48-file move worked 0.9 s on the floor's worker (it worked 4.5 s before that change), drawn in 164 ms; the window's longest stall in that step was 237 ms in L6b's New folder before the press, and 131 ms during the batch's Undo.
Fixed in place (L6b, marked 1.0 L6c): the DELETE room raised a TypeError whenever your home's bin was empty (the "Nothing deleted" words were %-formatted with the bin's name).

Sandbox words (K6) shortened for a folder's worth: ~/ paths, and Apply's answer summarised past three files ("16 new files in ~/Pictures/Camera, each read back and verified"); Apply's question lists five and "and N more"; "Undo the apply" on a row of its own (it was clipped at 1366x768).
findings_for_the_coordinator: Pre-existing stalls seen on the window's thread (not L6c): opening Downloads in the tree ~1.06 s (cabinet_qt.<lambda> .. locations.marker, X4 saw 855 ms); opening DELETE 300-360 ms (files_qt.show_trash); the K6 tab's show_utility ~500 ms and its run check ~300 ms (engineering_kernel.db on the window thread).

home_reach.area / home() resolve paths on every call; on this machine's deep throwaway paths files_service.may_change cost ~40 ms per call. Other per-file loops (L6b single moves, K2 file tools) would gain from reading the places once as bulk_files.Reach does.

K4/her plans do not offer files.batch (it is not a registered tool for her); the line's act and the tree are the owner's presses only. If her tidy plans (X3 everyday_desk) should move many files as one Undo, files.batch could be registered in tools_registry with a grant per folder.
